drop/layer: Here is a hidden layer's output, h: four units, with values two, one, three and two.
drop/mask: During training, dropout keeps each unit with probability p, here a half, and zeroes the rest. This time the random mask keeps units zero and two.
drop/zeroed: So the layer's output becomes two, zero, three, zero.
drop/scale: Then the kept units are divided by p. With p a half, that doubles them: four, zero, six, zero. This is inverted dropout.
drop/why: Why divide? A unit is kept only a fraction p of the time. Dividing by p makes up for it: on average, p times h over p is h, exactly what the unit gives without dropout.
test/test: At test time, every unit is kept and nothing is scaled. The layer passes h straight through: two, one, three, two.
test/match: Because training already divided by p, the next layer sees at test time what it saw on average in training. No correction is needed.
test/lean: And in training, any unit might vanish at any moment, so no unit can count on another being there. Each has to be useful on its own.
